### Problem: Majority Element {#sec-hash-p4-a}

::: {.p-statement}
Given $a$ of length $1 \le n \le 10^5$, return the majority element — the value occurring more than $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ times. **It always exists** in every input, so no "not found" case is needed.

Source: [LC 169 · Majority Element](https://leetcode.com/problems/majority-element/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
`Counter(a).most_common(1)` is the first thought and a fine implementation — but the follow-up is always the same: *"now do it in $O(1)$ memory."* The guarantee is the whole point: a value with more than half the copies **cannot be cancelled** if you repeatedly delete pairs of *distinct* elements — every deleted pair burns at most one of its copies while removing one non-majority, so majority copies always survive to the end (@sec-hash-vote). Boyer–Moore performs exactly those deletions without touching the array, tracking only "who is ahead, and by how much".
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Count everything.** Histogram with `Counter` (or a frequency array when the value range is small); return the argmax. $O(n)$.
2. **Sort and take the middle.** After sorting, the majority owns more than half the positions, so it must sit at index $n/2$. $O(n\log n)$ time, $O(1)$ extra space.
3. **Cancel pairs: Boyer–Moore.** One pass with `(cand, count)`: adopt when the counter is at zero, reinforce on agreement, burn one on disagreement. $O(n)$ time, $O(1)$ space; the invariant above is the proof.

**Invariant.** After any prefix, exactly `count` copies of `cand` are "standing", and every other element of the prefix has been removed in a pair of two different values. The majority value cannot be removed completely, because each removal takes at most one of its copies together with one of the fewer than $n/2$ other elements — so it is the candidate at the end.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Count everything, take the top

::: {.form-next}
The histogram reading of "more than $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$": count each value once, take the largest count. Straight, $O(n)$ expected, $O(n)$ memory — the memory is the only thing to fix.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
from collections import Counter

def majority_counter(a):
    return Counter(a).most_common(1)[0][0]
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <vector>
#include <unordered_map>
using namespace std;

int majorityElementCounter(vector<int>& a) {
    unordered_map<int, int> cnt;
    for (int x : a) ++cnt[x];
    pair<int, int> best = {0, 0};                 // {count, value}
    for (auto& e : cnt) best = max(best, make_pair(e.second, e.first));
    return best.second;
}
```
:::

#### Sort and take the middle

::: {.form-next}
Sort, then *observe* where the majority must be: more than half the indices belong to it, so the middle index $n/2$ is one of them. No counting at all — $O(1)$ extra space if you may reorder a copy.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def majority_sorted(a):
    s = sorted(a)
    return s[len(s) // 2]
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int majorityElementSorted(vector<int> a) {        // by value: we reorder it
    sort(a.begin(), a.end());
    return a[a.size() / 2];
}
```
:::

#### Cancel pairs: Boyer–Moore

::: {.form-next}
Replace the whole histogram by its *leaderboard*: `cand` and a `count`. At $0$ you adopt the current value; agreement adds one; disagreement cancels one `cand` against this different element — a deletion you are allowed to make because it removes at most one majority copy and one non-majority. The final `cand` is the majority, with no verification needed while the guarantee holds.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("majority", "vote")
    assert str(final) == "2"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: arr-majority-element
def majority_vote(a):
    cand, count = None, 0
    for x in a:
        if count == 0:
            cand, count = x, 1     # slot empty: adopt x
        elif x == cand:
            count += 1             # agree: reinforce
        else:
            count -= 1             # disagree: cancel one pair
    return cand                    # majority guaranteed - no verify pass


for _ in range(2000):              # build arrays where a majority MUST exist
    m = random.randint(1, 5)
    others = [o for o in (random.randint(1, 9) for _ in range(random.randint(0, 6)))
              if o != m]
    a = [m] * (len(others) + 1) + others
    random.shuffle(a)
    assert majority_vote(a) == majority_counter(a) == m

assert majority_vote([2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2]) == 2      # the board sample
assert majority_vote([3, 2, 3]) == 3                  # the LC examples
assert majority_vote([1]) == 1                        # n = 1
assert majority_sorted([2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2]) == 2    # the middle cell is the majority
print("majority_vote OK")
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr);
    int n; cin >> n;
    int cand = 0, count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        int x; cin >> x;                           // stream: no array needed
        if (count == 0)      { cand = x; count = 1; }
        else if (x == cand)  ++count;
        else                 --count;
    }
    cout << cand << '\n';        // the statement guarantees the majority exists
}
```
:::
:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Count everything, take the top** is $O(n)$ expected time and $O(n)$ space. **Sort and take the middle** is $O(n\log n)$ time, $O(1)$ extra space if a copy is allowed (in-place sort is $O(\log n)$ of stack). **Cancel pairs: Boyer–Moore** is $O(n)$ time, $O(1)$ space — the only form that meets the follow-up, and it reads the array once, so the C++ version above never stores it at all.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- $n = 1$: the single element wins; `count` adopts it at the first step.
- Two values tying near the line is impossible: $> \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ admits **at most one** winner — the reason one counter is enough.
- No guarantee (the interview twist): then `cand` may be a non-majority that merely survived; add a second counting pass over `cand` before returning it. That pass is *mandatory* in @sec-hash-p4-b.
- Every value equal: `count` just climbs to $n$.
:::

:::
